title: Senior asks: index.php uses catch (Throwable), not catch (Exception). What is the difference? What does this print?
explain: In PHP 7+, many engine errors (TypeError, ValueError) are Error objects, not Exception. catch (Exception) does not see them. Throwable is the parent of both. That is why the front controller catches Throwable: any failure becomes a clean 500 JSON, not a white page.
code:
<?php
function setLimit(int $n): void {}
try {
    setLimit('abc');
} catch (Exception $e) {
    echo 'Exception';
} catch (Throwable $e) {
    echo get_class($e);
}

title: Senior asks: a client sends {"price": 10.0, "qty": 2} to write on a .json file. The API decodes it and saves it again. What is in the file (compact)?
explain: json_decode gives price as float and qty as int. PHP 7.1+ json_encode writes a float with a decimal point (10.0). The int stays 2. The types survive the round trip, so the file keeps the same shape the client sent.

title: Senior asks: write() answers 201 when it creates a new file. What does the HTTP standard suggest to add to a 201 answer?
options: A Location header with the URL of the new file
An Allow header with the methods
explain: 201 Created means a new resource exists. The standard says the answer should tell where: a Location header (for example ?action=read&file=a.csv). Then the client does not need to guess the address. Allow belongs to 405, not to 201.

title: Senior asks: you want to test the CSV read with 8 bad inputs (BOM, empty file, duplicate headers...). The test code is the same, only the input changes. What do you use in PHPUnit?
options: A data provider method (#[DataProvider]) that returns the input sets
One test with a foreach inside it
A mock object for each input
explain: A data provider runs one test method once per input set. Each set is shown as its own result, so you see which input failed. A foreach inside one test stops at the first failure and hides the rest. Copied tests are hard to keep in sync.

title: #save is outside #list. After some minutes, one click on Save sends the data many times. Tap the bug.
explain: loadList runs every 5 seconds and adds one more click handler to #save each time. The old handlers stay. After a minute one click calls saveAll 12 times. Bind a handler once, outside the repeated function.

title: Works on your laptop. In production: Class "Faker\Factory" not found. src/ uses it, and composer.json has fakerphp/faker in require-dev. Why?
options: Production runs composer install --no-dev, so dev packages are not installed
Faker does not work on Linux
composer.lock is missing on the server
explain: require-dev packages are for tests and tools. The production deploy skips them with --no-dev. If code in src/ needs a package at run time, move it to require. Check: would the app run without this package? If not, it is not a dev dependency.

title: You have uncommitted changes. A teammate needs a quick fix on another branch. You want to keep your work safe, without a commit. Which command?
explain: git stash puts your changes on a shelf and gives you a clean working folder. Switch branches, fix, come back, then run git stash pop. reset --hard and checkout . delete your changes. --amend changes the last commit, which is not what you want.

title: What does this print (true/false for each line)?
explain: == on objects compares the class and all property values: $a and $b are equal. === asks if it is the same object. $a and $b are two objects, so false. $c is another handle to $a, so true. Use === when you need the same instance.
code:
<?php
class Point {
    public function __construct(public int $x) {}
}
$a = new Point(1);
$b = new Point(1);
$c = $a;
var_dump($a == $b, $a === $b, $a === $c);
